ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A certain fluorescent protein (GFP) emits green fluorescence under excitation by ultraviolet light or blue light, and this characteristic can be used to detect the expression of a target gene in cells. A certain scientific research team connected the coat protein (L1) gene of a certain virus to the 5′ end of the GFP gene, obtained the L1-GFP fusion gene (abbreviated as A), and inserted it into plasmid PO, constructing the eukaryotic expression vector P1. A schematic diagram of its partial structure and restriction sites is as follows. In the figure, the sticky ends produced by the four restriction enzymes E1-E4 are all different. According to the figure, infer that when the team inserted A into plasmid PO, it used two restriction enzymes. What are these two enzymes?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the schematic diagram, from left to right at the top are the four regions "promoter", "L1 gene", "GFP gene", and "terminator". Restriction enzyme sites are marked below: E1 is located near the junction between the promoter and the L1 gene, E2 is located near the junction between the L1 gene and the GFP gene, E3 is located within the GFP gene region, and E4 is located near the junction between the GFP gene and the terminator. Reasoning: in the question, A is the complete L1-GFP fusion gene formed by connecting the L1 gene to the 5′ end of the GFP gene. When inserting A into plasmid P0, the restriction sites at both ends of the fusion gene should be selected, both ensuring that the complete L1-GFP fragment is inserted and not destroying the coding sequences of L1 and GFP. E2 is near the connection between L1 and GFP, and E3 is inside GFP; using them would cut open the fusion gene or destroy the GFP sequence. Therefore, E1 at the upstream end of A and E4 at the downstream end should be selected.
